summary: Orchestrator window leak exposing opaque 429s for mixed-latency flows
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using PaperTrail's mixed workload (short interactive chat requests + hourly bulk embedding backfills) started seeing opaque 429s beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Errors appear tied to a specific dedicated pool and manifest as immediate 429 responses rather than queued rejects. Impacts: degraded ingestion for nightly backfills and intermittent failures for real-time chat during peak windows.

Impact:
- ~12% of batch embedding jobs during the 22:00-23:30 UTC window failed with 429 on the first request.
- Real-time latency-sensitive chat calls intermittently returned 429s for a subset of API keys belonging to the same org.
- Customer reports delays and automated retries caused duplication in downstream processing.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-06 (GPU: A100x8)
- Region: us-east
- API surface: REST v1 (POST /v1/embeddings, /v1/chat/completions)
- Rate limiting: tenant-level token windows + per-route micro-burst buckets enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Start 8 concurrent workers issuing 4k-token embedding batch requests in parallel across 8 API keys pinned to dp-us-east-06.
2. During the same time window, send steady interactive chat requests (~QPS 40) using a separate route but same tenant.
3. Observe that some embedding requests return 429 immediately with X-RateLimit-Reason: opaque_token_window

Logs / Observations:
- Gateway logs show immediate 429s with code rate_limit. No long queue wait recorded.
- Rate-limiter metric token_window_usage spiked and showed negative deltas when the orchestrator returned from a failed worker (possible double-debit).
- Edge proxy (nginx) traces show connection reuse between workers (keepalive) and a flurry of signed-url refreshes from the orchestrator at the same timestamps.
- No model-level throttles triggered in serving-runtime; GPU metrics show normal utilization.

Customer request:
- Wants explanation for opaque 429s and guidance to avoid data-loss/duplication while keeping throughput. Asks if a separate burst pool or different route isolation is recommended for mixed workloads.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:14 UTC - PaperTrail Ops: Noticed sudden first-request 429s during our midday backfill. We paused backfill and saw chat improve but still get sporadic 429s. Asked Redwood to investigate. (customer)

2026-03-10 11:02 UTC - Support L1 (Ellen Chen): Acknowledged and requested screenshots of 429 headers and client timestamps. Opened this ticket and escalated to L2. Note: customer on dedicated plan; flagged for SRE investigation.

2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - SRE (Diego Morales): Collected gateway logs and rate-limiter timeseries. Observed token_window_usage anomalies that correlate with orchestrator refresh events. Requested access to sample request IDs from customer and pool lease logs.

2026-03-11 03:20 UTC - PaperTrail Ops: Provided request-ids and a short packet capture of orchestrator control plane during the incident window. Also confirmed they were rotating ephemeral API keys during their ingest job.

2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - SRE (Diego Morales): Hypothesis: orchestrator-initiated ephemeral key rotation + keepalive connection reuse caused double-accounting of token debits at the edge rate-limiter. Preparing a mitigation patch to ensure idempotent debit when signed key renegotiation occurs.
2026-03-12 08:15 UTC - Support L2 (Ellen Chen): Provided recommended temporary config changes (see investigation notes) and asked customer to run a small test with burst pool separation.
2026-03-12 15:40 UTC - PaperTrail Ops: Ran the test. Bulk embedding reroutes to an isolated burst pool removed first-request 429s in the test window. Customer requests next steps for a permanent fix.

2026-03-12 17:00 UTC - SRE (Diego Morales): Noted plan to deploy a defensive fix to the orchestrator token accounting and follow with rate-limiter hardening. Scheduling follow-up release and postmortem link.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Ephemeral key rotation sequence during orchestrator worker handoffs generated parallel debit events at the edge. Edge sees two 'new' credentials and counts both against tenant window before backend handshake completed.
Hypothesis 2: Connection keepalive and HTTP/2 multiplexing allowed late signed-url refreshes to reuse streams that still carried earlier rate-limit context leading to misattributed token consumption.
Data points: token_window_usage and token_refund metrics show brief negative refunds aligning with orchestrator refresh timestamps (2026-03-09 22:07:31 UTC).
Test performed: Isolated embedding traffic to a dedicated burst pool for 30 minutes — immediate 429s disappeared for that route. Confirms separation reduces blast radius.

Relevant artifacts: gateway logs (s3://redwood-logs/SUP-1002024/gateway-2026-03-09.log), orchestrator control-plane trace (link in support workspace), rate-limiter dashboard panel (Confluence link included above).

Immediate mitigation options considered: 1) Separate route/burst pool for batch embeds; 2) Shorten ephemeral key rotation window; 3) Orchestrator patch to perform token-accounting in centralized step and return explicit refunds on failed handoffs.
resolution: Mitigation applied: recommended and assisted PaperTrail to create a separate burst pool for their hourly embed backfills; applied temporary smoothing policy to tenant token window to reduce immediate-first-request rejections. Engineering action: patch queued to ensure orchestrator refunds any partially-applied debits on worker handoff and to make signed-key negotiate idempotent for rate accounting. Postmortem to be published after fix rollout (tracking INT-10058). Follow-up items: deploy orchestrator patch, validate across dp-us-east-xx pools, and update docs with best-practice for mixed-latency workloads.
